description.narrative: Fair and inclusive economic creation as well as improving access to skill and education for disadvantaged women and youth is strategic pillar to Oxfam Somalia program to achieve that Oxfam program team identified the market needs for women in small business in terms financial and digital literacy. With this partnership with women right organization NAGAAD and local municipality we aim to create financial digital systems (ZAAD) as well as mobile digital literacy skill to women from marginalized backgrounds. The project would provide mobile phone devices and train to tab in the digital financial markets. Budget: 40 k USD include, literacy and numeracy skills training materials, distributing mobile devices , and mobile shopping carts . budget breakdown will be shared after Nagad partner and Oxfam Novib team agreed the implementation plan and project design. Methodology and partners Nagaad selected as implementingpartner, preliminary discussions done while NAGAAD supported same related initiatives enhancing literacy and numeracy of 80 women. Objective of the project – 2023 1. To empower economically the vulnerable small enterprises women in the market 2. Promote their capacity to use the mobile technology and money transfers. 3. To increase their literacy and numeracy skills for vulnerable women in small business to benefit and enable them to over come barriers to growth their small business 4. The target SMEs women will have better knowledge the growth of their business for the sustainable development in order to access finance and loans in the near future Detailed budget plan will be shared after the partner engagement meeting

participating-org.narrative: Nagaad is the women#s network in Somaliland, which ON has been supporting since its establishment in1997. Nagaad was formed by 32 women#s groups in Hargeisa. While it has raised its profile tremendously after 2000, with a range of advocacy and publicity actions in the media, notably around women#s political participation, it has always remained a of 32 member organisations, many of them remain weak, except for a few larger ones (some of whom are also counterparts of Oxfam Novib). Nagaad built its own office and received support from a variety of donors. Over the last four years Nagaad has elaborated a restructuring plan and a new strategic plan that involves: (a) more focus on networking instead of direct implementation; (b) admission of 15 new members from the regions of Somaliland, and working relationships with regional women#s umbrellas and professional associations. The network now has a membership of 46organisations.
